items.need: Your Stripe login. Five minutes. Nothing to pay.
steps: Go to dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys (link below).
Click "Create restricted key". Name it: Daraja launch

Set WRITE on exactly three things — Products, Prices, Payment links. Leave every other row on None. That means the key can create things and nothing else: it cannot move money, cannot refund, cannot see a customer.
Click Create, then Reveal, then copy the key.

Open Terminal on your Mac. Paste this line, REPLACE the words PASTE_KEY_HERE with your key, and only then press return:  mkdir -p ~/.daraja_secrets && printf '%s' 'PASTE_KEY_HERE' > ~/.daraja_secrets/stripe_key && chmod 600 ~/.daraja_secrets/stripe_key
Tell Claude "the key is in". He launches the first product and you watch a real Get it button appear in the store.

While you are on that security screen: add a PASSKEY (uses your fingerprint, nothing to buy, nothing to lose) and regenerate the BACKUP CODE — write those 24 characters on paper and put them in the fire safe. Never photograph it and never send it to anybody, including Claude.

items.t: Register darajastudio.com — at Cloudflare
items.why: Do this before the Meta step: a business website and email on your own domain help Meta verify Daraja Studio. Your free Cloudflare account already exists (made 7 Oct for the My Scores alerts), so just log in. You asked which one. Cloudflare, and it is not close. They sell domains AT COST with no markup, so it is about $10 a year forever — Namecheap shows a cheap first year then renews near $20. Over five years that is $55 against $110 for the identical domain. Cloudflare also gives you WHOIS privacy free and always on, which keeps your home address out of the public domain record; Namecheap sells that as an extra. And you will want Cloudflare anyway when the store moves off the GitHub address onto your own.
items.need: A credit card. About 12 minutes — a little longer than Namecheap because of one extra step.
steps: Go to cloudflare.com and make a free account. This is the extra step: Cloudflare will not sell you a domain until you have an account.

Search darajastudio.com. If it is taken, take darajastudio.co instead — then text me which one you got.
Buy ONE year. Turn auto-renew ON — a lapsed domain can be bought by anybody within days.
Ignore every upsell. You do not need their email, hosting or extra SSL. Privacy protection is already included and already on.
Tell me it is done. Pointing the store at it is a job for me, and takes about ten minutes.

items.t: 🧰 Try Business Manager yourself, as if you were a plumber
items.why: Before anyone else sees it, you should feel it the way a busy tradesman will. Everything you type stays on your own phone, and you can erase it all afterwards. Thirty minutes covers the whole loop: estimate → customer signs → receipt → invoice → paid.
items.need: Your iPhone, 30 minutes, and your own phone number (you'll play the customer too).
steps: Open the preview link (first button) in Safari on your iPhone. If it looks old or blank, wait two minutes and pull down to refresh.
Tap Share (the square with the arrow) → Add to Home Screen → Add. From now on open it from the 🧰 icon, not from Safari.

The welcome tour starts. Tap ▶ Start the tour and watch the example business (Miller Plumbing). At the end choose 🧪 Keep the examples and poke around for five minutes: Today, Jobs, + New, Money, More.
When you're ready to try it for real: on Today tap “Start my own business”. Answer the setup questions as a plumber with one helper (make up a name). Pick PayPal or Zelle so invoices get Pay buttons.
Tap + → New job. Customer: YOUR OWN name and YOUR mobile number. Job: “Replace kitchen faucet”. Save.
Tap ➕ Add item and pick two things from the price list. Then tap 📨 Send estimate → 💬 Text it. Messages opens with the text filled in — send it to yourself.
Open that text on your phone (you are now the customer). Sign in the box with your finger, tick the box, tap ✅ Approve this estimate. Your phone writes an approval text back — send it (to yourself).

Open that approval text and tap its link. You should see “✅ … signed it — saved to the job”. If it opened in Safari and says it can't find the estimate: tap 📋 Copy this link, open the 🧰 app, open the job, tap 👍 They said yes, paste it in the box at the bottom.
Take any store receipt from your wallet. Tap + → 📸 Receipt → Take a picture. Check the items it read, pick “Most of this is for” = your faucet job, mark one item 🍫 Personal, tap Save receipt.
On the job, tap ✅ Work is done → 🧾 Bill it → 📨 Send invoice with pay link → send it to yourself. Open it as the customer and look at the Pay buttons (don't pay).
Back in the app tap 💵 Record a payment → Save. The job closes itself. Open Money to see it counted.
Tap 📝 To-do → 📋 Add common due dates. Tick the ones that fit you and add your real truck registration date.
Anything confusing, slow or wrong: write it down, or just tell Claude “Business Manager: …” — every note becomes a fix.
When you're done: More → Erase everything and start over (or keep it — it's only on your phone).

items.t: 🔮 Zuri, later: incoming calls with AI answering, outage texts, marketing — the hooks
items.why: Jerry's thinking, 1 Oct. All three stand on the same four hooks: (1) an SMS and voice account with Africa's Talking (Kenyan numbers, ~KES 0.80 a text; sender ID ZURI needs Safaricom approval) — unlocks reminder texts, outage alerts and marketing; (2) a messages log on every customer (every text in and out, every call) plus a “no texts” tick and consent; (3) the Company & hubs setup (areas with pins, hub phone numbers) so an outage can say “Zuri B, near the market, back by 4pm” and text only those customers; (4) an inbound door — an edge function that receives call events and text replies, looks the caller up by number, and lets the Zuri manager open a job or answer. AI answering = Africa's Talking voice → speech-to-text → Claude (the same pattern as the Zuri manager) → text-to-speech; start with a text bot (“reply BALANCE”) before voice. Marketing = the same sending door, with segments we already have (area, package, paid/late, leads) and templates in English and Swahili. Order I'd build: SMS account → reminders + outage texts → company & hubs → inbound text bot → voice.
